The Discussion on the Realm of Non-percipient Beings:
Is the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling associated with the realm of non-percipient beings?
Yes, it is.

Is there, for one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, the wholesome root of non-greed, the wholesome root of non-hatred, the wholesome root of non-delusion, as well as faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom?
You should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is it not the case that, for one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, there is no wholesome root of non-greed, no wholesome root of non-hatred... [and so on] ... nor wisdom?
“Yes,” you say.

But if for one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling there is no root of the wholesome consisting of non-greed, no root of the wholesome consisting of non-hatred, no root of the wholesome consisting of non-delusion, nor faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, or wisdom,
then indeed it should not be said that “the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling belongs to the non-percipient beings.”
Is the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling the same as the state of non-percipient beings? Yes.
Does one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling possess contact, feeling, perception, volition, and consciousness? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there no contact,
feeling, perception, volition, or consciousness for one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling? Yes.
Is there development of the path for one without contact? ... Is there development of the path for one without mind?
One should not say so...
Is it not the case that there is development of the path for one with contact? ... Is there development of the path for one with mind?
“Yes.

[The opponent asks: “If the cultivation of the path belongs to one who possesses contact … [and] if the cultivation of the path belongs to one who possesses mind, then indeed, sir, you should not say:”
“The attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling belongs to the non-percipient beings.
Is it the case that the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling belongs to the non-percipient beings?
Yes, it is.
Are all those who enter the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling necessarily beings of the non-percipient realm?
You should not say so... [and so on]...
It should not be said.
“Is the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling [a state] belonging to non-percipient beings?”—
Yes. But is it not the case that here too one is non-percipient, and there too one is non-percipient?
“Yes.
“If one is non-percipient here and also non-percipient there, then indeed it must be said:
‘The attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling belongs to the non-percipient beings.’”
The Discussion on the Non-percipient Beings is finished.
